prior_exception.reason: The defining 120 EC in years one and two is chemistry and laboratory centred: analytical, organic and inorganic chemistry; molecular structure and bonding; thermodynamics, quantum mechanics and physics; successive chemical synthesis and analysis laboratories. In year three, at least 12 EC of chemistry electives and a 12-EC independent chemistry research internship/report remain required. Although 27 EC can be freely chosen, UCR lacks a chemistry gateway and any stand-alone introductory or advanced organic, inorganic, analytical, physical or synthetic chemistry sequence. A 24-course UCR route using biology, geoscience, statistics and programming would have too little chemistry and would misrepresent the programme’s academic core.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The official prospective year-one page is labelled 2027–28 while the year-two and year-three pages are indicative 2026–27; these are a present programme structure cross-check, not a guaranteed cohort contract. Summing positive-credit items yields 60 EC in each year. Year-three 9 EC taught compulsory work plus 12 EC compulsory internship plus 39 EC elective room = 60 EC; 12 of the latter is restricted to Chemistry electives, with 27 EC free. The education minor is optional, and alternative chemistry electives are not simultaneously required.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Checked all 151 enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, profile/topic enrichment, prerequisites and planned terms. HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry and HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory provide biochemical content and molecular lab work, while HCBGATE101 and HCBLIFE211 introduce life science and cells. ENSENVI311 Environmental Biogeochemistry and ENSDELT311 R3: Recycling, Recovery, Remediation touch geochemical/inorganic processes and recovery; ENSSUST112 and ENSSUST211 address materials life cycles and energy systems. DISGATE102, DISMATH211/214/314 and DISGATE101 provide some mathematical, statistical and programming support. None provides the laboratory and theory progression in chemical analysis, organic/inorganic synthesis, physical chemistry, molecular spectroscopy and quantum chemistry required to underpin this bachelor and its independent chemistry research internship. Isolated biochemical and environmental chemistry coverage cannot support a defensible 24-course Chemistry match.

prior_exception.reason: This mathematics degree requires a broad proof-based progression: 51 EC in a dense first-year mathematical core, an additional required 6 EC multivariable analysis and 18 EC in differential equations, rings/fields and topology in the selected line, then 30 EC more upper mathematics (18 restricted line electives and 12 additional mathematics electives), plus a 12-EC independent mathematics thesis, seminar and modelling work. UCR offers introductory and applied mathematics, statistics, programming and data science but lacks sustained stand-alone real/complex analysis, abstract algebra and topology at the required depth. Substituting AI and data-science courses for the upper mathematical sequence would misrepresent the defining Mathematics identity, despite substantial overlap in applied computational methods.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The selected first-listed line is Mathematics, not the differently required Applied Mathematics or Probability and Statistics lines. Year 1=51 EC compulsory+9 EC free; years 2–3=12 EC common year-two courses+48 EC Mathematics line (18 prescribed, 18 restricted choices, 12 supplemental mathematics)+24 EC year-three fixed seminar/practicum/portfolio/thesis+36 EC genuinely free. The 3-EC first-listed course from the dedicated elective page meets its second-year selection rule. Exact elective allocations by year are illustrative and must respect the current online catalogue/OER. Public year-one/two pages give 2026–27 and year-three gives 2027–28 indicative offerings.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows with descriptions, prerequisites, profiles and planned terms. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods introduces calculus and linear algebra; DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems, DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics and DISARIN212 Logic & Discrete Mathematics provide relevant but predominantly introductory or applied coverage. DISGATE101 Programming and DISDATA111/211/311 add computational/data-science methods. There is no dedicated UCR sequence in real and complex analysis, rings and fields, topology, functional analysis, number theory or mathematics-specific independent thesis sufficient for this 180-EC route. Cross-disciplinary electives cannot fill the restricted 48-EC Mathematics line without changing the subject of the comparison.

prior_exception.curriculumContext: The authoritative current TU Delft sources establish a full-time, broad 180-EC bachelor organised over three academic years. prior_exception.reason: Automotive Technology is an integrated electrical, mechanical, computational and control-engineering degree. Its compulsory formation moves from mathematics, computation, signals, systems, dynamics, electromagnetics, electronics and electromechanics into power electronics, sensing and actuation, electric and hybrid powertrain design, road-vehicle dynamics, vehicle networking, control systems, automotive software engineering, autonomous driving, automotive projects and a Bachelor Final Project. UCR offers useful mathematics, programming, data science, image processing, AI, robotics, linear systems, consumer-product design and sustainable-energy courses. It does not provide the required physics and electrical-engineering progression, vehicle mechanics and dynamics, electric-powertrain engineering, embedded and real-time automotive systems, vehicle communications, engineering laboratories, staged automotive design projects or an equivalent automotive capstone. A UCR pathway could address intelligent mobility, vehicle data and sustainable transport as an interdisciplinary theme, but it would not be a defensible Automotive Technology comparator.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The official current curriculum structure accounts for the full 180 EC: 120 EC of automotive major and Bachelor College core formation, including the Bachelor Final Project, plus a 60-EC elective part consisting of a 15-EC USE/ITEC learning line and 45 EC of electives. The major-course pages identify a deliberately integrated engineering spine: computation and mathematics; signals, systems and dynamics; electromagnetics, electronics, electromechanics and power electronics; sensing and actuation; electric and hybrid powertrain design; road-vehicle dynamics; vehicle networking; control systems; automotive software engineering; autonomous driving; projects; and the final project. The live programme page characterises the vehicle as a controlled high-tech system combining mechanics, electronics, sensors and informatics rather than as a general transport or sustainability subject.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics provide relevant quantitative foundations. DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming, DISCOMP213 Software Development, DISDATA111 Introduction to Data Science, DISDATA211 Machine Learning, DISDATA212 Image Processing & Computer Vision, DISDATA311 Neural Networks & Deep Learning and DISDATA312 Robotics support computation, perception, planning and general control-related work. BENENTR111 Consumer Product Design adds team-based product development, while ENSGATE101 Sustainability Essentials I, ENSSUST112 Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy, ENSSUST211 Energy & Sustainability and ENSSUST311 Renewable System Design support environmental and energy perspectives. The workbook nevertheless contains no mechanics or vehicle-dynamics sequence, electromagnetics, circuit and electronics sequence, electromechanical energy conversion, power electronics, electric or hybrid powertrain design, automotive sensing-and-actuation laboratory, embedded systems, real-time automotive software, in-vehicle networking, automotive safety and reliability engineering, vehicle-systems integration project, or automotive Bachelor Final Project. DISMATH312 studies linear systems from an engineering perspective but cannot replace the target's staged control, electronics and vehicle laboratories. DISDATA212 and DISDATA312 cover general computer vision and robotics rather than automotive perception hardware, vehicle networking and validated autonomous-driving systems. The available UCR courses therefore support an interdisciplinary intelligent-mobility theme while leaving the target programme's defining physical-engineering, embedded-systems, laboratory and capstone formation unmatched.

prior_exception.curriculumContext: The current official structure accounts for the full 180 EC: 105 EC of compulsory biomedical-engineering study, a 15-EC Bachelor Final Project, a 15-EC USE/ITEC learning line and 45 EC of free electives. Current laboratory education includes chemical-biology skills, cell and biomaterial experimentation, biomedical imaging and data analysis, biomechanics, tissue engineering and cell-based challenges. The final project requires students to formulate, execute and report a small-scale research study in a TU/e research group.

HCBGATE101 Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, HCBLIFE211 Molecular Cell Biology, HCBLIFE212 Human Physiology, HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry, HCBLIFE311 Molecular Pathology & Genetics, HCBBIOM211 Functional Anatomy, HCBBIOM311 Pharmacology, HCBBIOM312 Infection & Immunity and HCBBIOM313 Mechanisms of Disease provide strong biomedical foundations. The workbook nevertheless contains no general-physics sequence for biomedical engineering, electromagnetism, mechanics and biomechanics progression, stress-strain and constitutive modelling of biological tissue, biomaterials, mechanobiology, tissue engineering or biofabrication, biomedical sensors and instrumentation, physiological signal-acquisition laboratory, optical and medical-imaging physics, biomedical device-design studio, or advanced experimental sequence integrating cells, materials and engineered systems. prior_exception.reason: TU/e's AUBS bachelor is a project- and studio-intensive built-environment engineering degree. Its common first year integrates calculus, architecture and the city, urban systems, healthy and sustainable environments, structural statics, circularity and energy performance, and structure and architecture with four successive design or research projects. The later programme requires one of four coherent tracks and its project sequence: architectural and urban design, building physics and services, structural engineering and design, or urban systems and real estate. All routes culminate in multidisciplinary project work and a discipline-specific Bachelor End Project. UCR offers useful adjacent courses in spatial planning, GIS and earth observation, sustainable energy and life-cycle analysis, nature-based design, product design, heritage and quantitative methods. It has no architecture or urban-design studio sequence, building-physics and building-services sequence, structural statics and materials progression, construction-technology education, architectural drawing and modelmaking formation, or built-environment engineering capstone. A 24-course UCR programme would therefore replace the target's defining studio, technical and project spine with adjacent liberal-arts and sustainability study and would not be an academically defensible comparison.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The official 2026-2027 AUBS guide and current Education Guide account for all 180 EC as 130 EC core, 40 EC electives and 10 EC ITEC. Year one is common and explicitly orients students across AUDE, BPS, SED and USRE through built-environment courses and four projects. In years two and three, students choose one track, complete its core courses and projects, and use genuine elective space for depth, cross-track study or a thematic profile. The current guide requires a multidisciplinary project before the 10-EC Bachelor End Project. Illustrative named course and project lists include Histories of Architecture and Urbanism, Architecture and Technology, Dimensioning of Structures, Urban Planning, Building Services, Concrete and Masonry Structures, Steel and Timber Structures and Applied Mechanics, Building Performance, Urban Physics, Sustainable Retrofit, Regenerative Building Design, structural and architectural design projects, urban-mobility projects and the final disciplinary project. The aggregate 130-EC core component preserves the complete degree without pretending that four mutually exclusive tracks are simultaneously compulsory.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook rows, including names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. ENSDELT111 Building with Nature supplies one nature-based engineering and design course; ENSSUST315 Spatial Planning and ENSENVI211 Earth Observation provide spatial planning, GIS, remote sensing and geospatial analysis; ENSSUST112 Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy, ENSSUST211 Energy & Sustainability and ENSSUST311 Renewable System Design provide environmental-performance and systems perspectives; ENSENVI112 Natural Hazards, ENSENVI212 Soils & Aquifers and ENSENVI311 Environmental Biogeochemistry add environmental context; BENENTR111 Consumer Product Design provides a product-development project; MCCHEAM111, MCCHEAM212 and MCCHEAM315 address art, architectural history, heritage and material culture; and UCR mathematics, data and research-methods courses supply transferable analysis. These are valuable adjacent offerings, but the workbook contains no architectural or urban-design studio sequence, architectural drawing and physical modelmaking, building structures and applied mechanics sequence, concrete/steel/timber design, building physics, lighting/acoustics and services engineering, construction technology, façade and roof materialisation, real-estate and urban-development project sequence, multidisciplinary building-design project, or 10-EC built-environment Bachelor End Project. prior_exception.curriculumContext: The supported first year covers human origins and Near Eastern prehistory; European prehistory and Classical archaeology; historical archaeology and the Americas; natural and cultural landscapes; material studies; field techniques and a field school; museum and site heritage; archaeological data analysis; and disciplinary history and future practice. The current OER confirms 150 EC of compulsory study and up to 30 EC of optional study for the 180-EC programme, but the prospectus does not identify the remaining 120 EC for the new generic cohort separately from legacy specialisation groups. Because the external-programme gate fails, no terminal UCR match assessment or UCR alternative is published. Revisit the target when Leiden publishes the later-year requirements for the post-specialisation curriculum.

prior_exception.reason: Leiden Bio-Pharmaceutical Sciences is an integrated experimental drug-science degree. Its compulsory spine combines general and organic chemistry, molecular and cell biology, biochemistry, physiology, genetics, pharmacology, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics, ADME, toxicology, bio-analysis, drug design and synthesis, biopharmacy and biophysics, multiple discipline-specific laboratories, modern drug development, a 30-EC specialisation and a 16-EC bachelor research project. The selected broad route adds pharmaceutical formulation and analysis, technology, quality and pharmacotherapy. UCR offers a strong molecular-biomedical cluster, one pharmacology course, quantitative and data-science methods, and one life-science laboratory, but no chemistry sequence, medicinal or pharmaceutical chemistry, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics, drug-design and synthesis sequence, pharmaceutical analysis, formulation science, pharmaceutical technology and quality, staged drug-science laboratories or comparable bio-pharmaceutical research capstone. A 24-course UCR programme would therefore become general biomedical science rather than a defensible Bio-Pharmaceutical Sciences comparator.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The live 2026-2027 Leiden curriculum accounts for exactly 180 EC: 60 EC of compulsory first-year foundations, 60 EC of compulsory second-year drug-science and biomedical study, and a third year comprising 14 EC of compulsory academic and modern-drug-development work, the selected 30-EC Bio-Pharmaceutical Sciences and Pharmacy specialisation and a 16-EC bachelor research project. The specialisation is selected under the broad-academic-identity rule before UCR fit is considered.

HCBGATE101 Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, HCBLIFE211 Molecular Cell Biology, HCBLIFE212 Human Physiology, HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry, HCBLIFE311 Molecular Pathology & Genetics, HCBBIOM211 Functional Anatomy, HCBBIOM311 Pharmacology, HCBBIOM312 Infection & Immunity and HCBBIOM313 Mechanisms of Disease provide substantial molecular, physiological, disease and medicines foundations. HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory adds biochemical and molecular laboratory work, including bacterial techniques, protein production, DNA analysis and basic bioinformatics. HCBPSYC211 Statistics & Experimental Methods, DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics, DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming, DISDATA111 Introduction to Data Science and DISDATA211 Machine Learning provide transferable quantitative and computational support. The workbook contains no general- or organic-chemistry sequence, medicinal or pharmaceutical chemistry, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics, ADME course, bio-analysis of drugs, drug-design and synthesis sequence, biopharmacy and formulation science, pharmaceutical technology or quality, pharmacotherapy sequence, organic-synthesis or pharmaceutical-analysis laboratory, staged drug-development practical formation, or 16-EC bio-pharmaceutical research project. HCBBIOM311 is one broad pharmacology course and HCBLIFE214 one life-science laboratory; together with the strong biomedical cluster they still cannot replace the target's chemistry, drug-design, dosage-form, analytical and experimental-pharmacy spine. No academically honest 24-course closest match can therefore be formed.

prior_exception.reason: Leiden Chinese Studies is an integrated area-studies and language degree. Its defining core contains a cumulative modern Mandarin sequence, classical Chinese, Chinese-language source work, Chinese history and culture across premodern and modern periods, contemporary Chinese politics, economics and society, region-specific disciplinary choices, an intensive study period in China or Taiwan and an independent Chinese Studies paper. UCR offers strong general courses in history, politics, international relations, sociology, economics, literature, media, philosophy and cultural heritage, but it offers no Mandarin or classical Chinese language sequence, no Chinese-language source training, no China- or East-Asia-focused course sequence and no comparable situated study or Chinese Studies research environment. A 24-course UCR programme would therefore replace the programme's defining language-and-area formation with adjacent general disciplines rather than constitute a defensible Chinese Studies comparison.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The live 2026-2027 Leiden curriculum accounts for exactly 180 EC across three 60-EC years. The represented pathway preserves 55 EC of Year 1 compulsory work plus one 5-EC bound elective; 25 EC of Year 2 compulsory work, 15 EC of selected China-focused content, one 5-EC shared East Asia course and one 15-EC Mandarin 2c option; and 10 EC of compulsory third-year Mandarin, one 5-EC language option, one 5-EC content option, a 10-EC BA paper and 30 EC of open elective space. There is no formal route. The restricted choices instantiate one coherent political-economy-and-society emphasis without changing the programme's broad identity.

GOSHIST111 Modern History, GOSHIST211 History of Empires and GOSHIST312 History Research Seminar provide historical frameworks and research practice; GOSPOLI112 Foundations of Comparative Politics, GOSPOLI212 Theory of International Relations, BENECON111 Introduction to Economics, BENECON211 International Macroeconomics, BENENTR312 International Business & Governance, GOSSOCI111 Introduction to Sociology, GOSSOCI214 Modern Sociology and GOSSOCI212 Qualitative Research Methodology support political, economic and social analysis; MCCLITR111 Introduction to Literary Studies, MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature, MCCMEDI111 Introduction to Film & Media, MCCMEDI311 Media & Race, MCCHEAM111 Introduction to Western Art History and GOSPHIL111 Introduction to Western Philosophy provide general cultural, literary, media, heritage and philosophical study. These are transferable disciplinary perspectives, not China-specific courses. The workbook contains no Mandarin course, classical Chinese, Chinese linguistics, Chinese history, Chinese literature, Chinese philosophy or religion, Chinese politics or economy, East Asian regional studies, Chinese-language primary-source training, China/Taiwan study component or Chinese Studies research capstone. It therefore cannot support an academically honest 24-course closest match.

prior_exception.reason: Leiden is phasing in a revised Criminology curriculum. The current 2026-2027 Study Guide establishes the revised first and second years, but it expressly labels the displayed third year as the old curriculum for students who began in 2024 or earlier and states that Year 3 of the revised curriculum will only be published in the 2027-2028 guide. Combining the 120 EC revised sequence with the 60 EC legacy third year would create a pathway that no Fall 2026 entrant can follow. The missing applicable third-year structure cannot be inferred from the outgoing curriculum without inventing compulsory, elective, research and thesis requirements.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The applicable revised curriculum is supported for 120 EC: 60 EC in Year 1 and 60 EC in Year 2, each composed of twelve compulsory 5-EC modules. It establishes integrated criminological theory, legal and criminal-justice study, psychological and sociological explanations, qualitative and quantitative methods, professional skills, policy evaluation, victims and offenders, cybercrime, investigation and prosecution, forensic psychology and experimental methods. The current product confirms that the programme as a whole is 180 EC, but the remaining revised 60 EC are not yet published. The legacy Year 3 shown in the same product is deliberately excluded because Leiden restricts it to earlier cohorts.

The official product confirms that the bachelor as a whole is 180 EC, but its displayed 60-EC third year is an outgoing structure and the replacement curriculum for the Fall 2026 cohort is not yet published.

cases.ucr_reassessment: Separate UCR assessment required; superseded no-match judgment is preserved below.

prior_exception.reason: Leiden French Language and Culture is a cumulative French-medium language-and-humanities degree. Its defining compulsory formation integrates sustained advanced French speaking, listening and academic writing through C1 with grammar, syntax, phonology, French linguistics, literature across historical periods, French and Francophone cultural history, programme-specific research seminars and a French-focused thesis. UCR offers strong English-medium courses in literary, communication, film, media, historical and cultural analysis plus one psycholinguistics course, but it has no taught French-language acquisition sequence and no French or Francophone studies curriculum. A 24-course UCR pathway could study literature, media, identity and postcolonial questions comparatively, but it could not preserve the target's academic identity as French Language and Culture.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The official curriculum accounts for the full 180 EC as 60 EC of fixed first-year French language, linguistics, literature and culture study; 80 EC of upper-year programme-specific language and humanities formation; 30 EC of genuine free-choice space; and a 10-EC BA thesis. The current cohort rules require multiple French-programme seminars, including research seminars, alongside advanced written and oral language work. Leiden's official programme material states that classes are French-medium and foregrounds the Francophone world beyond France. Even after the 30-EC free-choice block is preserved, the remaining 150 EC form a connected French-proficiency and French/Francophone-studies core rather than a collection of general humanities electives.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 records in the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx (SHA-256 7bf6c2ae9de0837086ec741c27bd94ed7e85dff2d25bde619ecd50cc4d685879), including names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned availability. MCCLITR111 Introduction to Literary Studies, MCCLITR112 Great Literary Works, MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature, MCCLITR212 Life & Travel Writing, MCCLITR311 Film & Text and MCCLITR312 Perspectives on Literary Meaning provide substantial comparative literary study. MCCCOMM211 Style & Meaning adds linguistic and close-reading methods; HCBCOGN312 Psycholinguistics studies language acquisition, use and comprehension; and the communication, film, media, history, sociology and heritage offerings support analysis of culture, identity, colonialism, decolonial critique and representation. The workbook nevertheless contains no French-language course at any level, no staged speaking, listening, grammar, phonetics or academic-writing sequence in French, no French linguistics, no historical sequence in French literature, no dedicated French or Francophone cultural-studies course, no French-medium research seminar and no French-focused thesis. Psycholinguistics is a general cognitive-science course rather than language instruction, and the literature and media courses are comparative English-medium offerings rather than a French/Francophone disciplinary spine. No academically honest 24-course closest match can therefore supply the target programme's cumulative language proficiency and area-specific formation.

prior_exception.reason: Leiden Medicine is an integrated medical-professional bachelor whose defining formation combines cellular and organ-system science with disease mechanisms, clinically oriented patient problems, pharmacology, longitudinal medical progress testing, patient communication, professional behaviour, care-stage and early-practice contact, clinical reasoning, history taking and physical examination. UCR offers a strong biomedical, behavioural and public-health curriculum, but no supervised patient-care placement, clinical examination and history-taking sequence, integrated diagnostic-reasoning progression, longitudinal medical-professional assessment or comprehensive clinically organized organ-system curriculum. A 24-course UCR programme could provide excellent preparation in biomedical and health sciences, but it would not be a defensible Medicine comparator.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The latest complete official programme table accounts for exactly 180 EC: 60 EC per year. Year 1 integrates normal cellular, molecular and organ-system structure and function with a care internship, academic/scientific training, communication and professional skills, ethics, law, prevention, health promotion, technology and the medical progress test. Year 2 advances through disease mechanisms, pharmacology and integrated clinical-problem blocks supported by longitudinal academic and professional formation. Year 3 preserves 15 EC of genuine faculty elective space and combines reproduction, mental health and hormones, ageing and emergency-care problem blocks with clinical skills, early practice contacts, academic critical appraisal and the progress test. The bachelor endpoint is distributed across assessed clinical and research outputs rather than isolated as one separately credited thesis.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 records in the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx (SHA-256 7bf6c2ae9de0837086ec741c27bd94ed7e85dff2d25bde619ecd50cc4d685879), including names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned availability. HCBGATE101 Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, HCBLIFE211 Molecular Cell Biology, HCBLIFE212 Human Physiology, HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry, HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory and HCBLIFE311 Molecular Pathology & Genetics provide substantial biomedical foundations. HCBBIOM211 Functional Anatomy, HCBBIOM311 Pharmacology, HCBBIOM312 Infection & Immunity and HCBBIOM313 Mechanisms of Disease add advanced biomedical content; HCBGATE102 Introduction to Brain & Behavior and the cognition and psychology sequences cover neural, behavioural and mental-health perspectives; HCBBIOM111 Epidemiology & Public Health, HCBPSYC311 Medical & Health Psychology and quantitative research courses add population, behavioural and evidence perspectives. The workbook nevertheless contains no supervised clinical placement or patient-care course, no patient interviewing and physical-examination sequence, no longitudinal clinical-skills assessment, no integrated diagnostic-reasoning curriculum, no medicine-wide progress testing, and no comprehensive clinical-problem progression across organ systems and life stages. The available biomedical courses therefore support a biomedical-science alternative, not the profession-defining academic and clinical formation of Medicine.

prior_exception.reason: Leiden Classics is defined by cumulative ancient Greek and Latin language acquisition, sustained reading of prose and poetry in both original languages, philological and linguistic analysis, and advanced independent reading and research across the two languages. UCR offers valuable study of ancient history, archaeology, philosophy, literature, myth, art and reception, but no Greek or Latin language-acquisition sequence and no curriculum of primary classical texts in the original languages. Those are not peripheral specialist additions: they organize the Leiden programme from the first year through the thesis. A UCR ancient-world pathway would therefore be a defensible Ancient Studies programme, but not a defensible comparator for this language-and-philology-centred Classics degree.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The latest complete official programme table accounts for exactly 180 EC: 60 EC per year. Year 1 contains 20 EC of Greek and Latin language acquisition and 20 EC of original-language prose, rhetoric, drama and lyric/elegy, integrated with ancient history, philosophy, literary theory and literary history. Year 2 continues Greek and Latin texts, epic, drama, Greek linguistics and Renaissance Latin while adding material culture, source transmission, philosophy of science and a restricted ancient-philosophy choice. Year 3 preserves 30 EC of genuine free choice and requires 15 EC of advanced Greek/Latin reading, late-antique philosophy and religion, and a 10-EC thesis; both classical languages must remain represented.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 records in the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx (SHA-256 7bf6c2ae9de0837086ec741c27bd94ed7e85dff2d25bde619ecd50cc4d685879), including names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned availability. MCCHEAM112 Introduction to World Archaeology, MCCHEAM213 Greek Archaeology, MCCHEAM315 Heritage & Ancient Democracy, GOSHIST213 Western Way of War, GOSPHIL111 Introduction to Western Philosophy, MCCLITR111 Introduction to Literary Studies, MCCLITR112 Great Literary Works and MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature provide substantial ancient-world, philosophical, literary and material-culture perspectives; MCCHEAM212 Renaissance Italy & Global Mediterranean and MCCCOMM111 The Art of Rhetorical Communication support reception and rhetoric. The workbook nevertheless contains no ancient Greek course, no Latin course, no cumulative grammar and vocabulary sequence, no sustained original-language reading of Greek and Roman prose and poetry, no classical philology or Greek linguistics sequence, and no advanced Greek/Latin independent reading. Because those missing elements constitute the degree's continuous disciplinary spine, the available ancient-history, archaeology and literature courses support Ancient Studies rather than a defensible Classics match.

prior_exception.reason: Leiden International Studies is not merely a broad collection of global politics, economics, history and culture courses. Every student selects one world region, studies that region through all four disciplinary perspectives, completes a cumulative 25-EC associated-language sequence plus a 5-EC language-and-culture-in-practice course, and writes an area-specific thesis. UCR offers strong adjacent work in international relations, economics, history, law, sociology, media and sustainability, but its current curriculum contains only one general Dutch course and no sustained regional-language sequence. It also lacks a coherent four-perspective area curriculum for any one of the eight Leiden regions. Filling 24 UCR slots with globally oriented courses would therefore reproduce breadth while discarding the degree's defining language-plus-regional-specialisation architecture.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The latest complete official study-guide table accounts for exactly 180 EC: 60 EC per year. Year 1 establishes academic literacy, cultural studies, economics, politics, sociolinguistics and world history, then begins a selected region through culture/language, history and 10 EC of language acquisition. Year 2 adds the region's economy and politics, cross-cultural communication, research methods, global political economy, international relations, philosophy of science, a thematic seminar and 15 further EC in the same language. Year 3 contains 30 EC of genuine elective space and requires a 10-EC consultancy project, 5 EC of language and culture in practice, and a 15-EC area-specific thesis. Africa with Arabic is instantiated only by the official-order tie-break; the same structural mismatch applies to all eight areas and their linked languages.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 records in the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx (SHA-256 7bf6c2ae9de0837086ec741c27bd94ed7e85dff2d25bde619ecd50cc4d685879), including names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned availability. BENECON111 Introduction to Economics, BENECON211 International Macroeconomics, GOSPOLI212 Theory of International Relations, GOSPOLI313 Peace & Conflict, GOSHIST111 Modern History, GOSHIST211 History of Empires, GOSLAWJ111 Human Rights: Law & Philosophy, GOSLAWJ212 Introduction to Public International Law, GOSSOCI212 Qualitative Research Methodology and ENSDELT312 Governance of Sustainability cover much of the global economics, politics, history, justice, methods and sustainability breadth. MCCHEAM211 African Art & Heritage and MCCMEDI311 Media & Race provide valuable regionally relevant cultural perspectives, while BENENTR312 International Business & Governance and the communication curriculum support international professional applications. However, the workbook has no Arabic course and no cumulative foreign-language pathway; MCCCOMM112 Dutch is the only named language-acquisition course. It also has no four-course Africa sequence spanning culture/language, history, economy and politics, and no language-in-practice course or area-specific thesis seminar. Other Leiden routes face the same absence of a linked 30-EC language progression and coherent regional spine. These omissions affect the organizing structure of all three years and cannot be repaired through the 30-EC elective space.

prior_exception.reason: Leiden Italian Language and Culture is organized around cumulative Italian proficiency and sustained Italian-language study of linguistics, literature, culture and society. Its compulsory sequence progresses from Lingua italiana Ia/Ib/Ic through IIa/IIb, while subject courses cover Italian phonology, morphology, syntax, language history and variation, medieval through contemporary literature, and Italian cultural history. The thesis may be written in Italian. UCR offers strong adjacent humanities courses, including one focused on Renaissance Italy, but no Italian language instruction, no Italian-language source-analysis sequence and no Italian linguistics. A 24-course UCR pathway in general European history, literature, film, communication and art would therefore replace the degree's continuous language-and-area core rather than provide a defensible comparator.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The latest complete official programme accounts for exactly 180 EC: fixed 60-EC first and second years, followed by 20 EC of Italian subject work, 30 EC of genuine free choice and a 10-EC BA thesis in Year 3. Year 1 contains 20 EC of Italian proficiency alongside Italian literature, culture, linguistics and Romance linguistics. Year 2 contains 20 further EC of Italian proficiency plus Italian poetry, contemporary language, present-day Italy, Dante, modern literature, history of Italian and a subject research paper. Year 3 continues Italian literature and linguistics through fixed and monographic courses before the thesis. The official programme outcomes target high Italian proficiency, analysis of Italian phonology, morphology, syntax and semantics, recognition of historical, geographical and sociolinguistic variants, and knowledge of Italian literary and cultural history.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 records in the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx (SHA-256 7bf6c2ae9de0837086ec741c27bd94ed7e85dff2d25bde619ecd50cc4d685879), including names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned availability. MCCHEAM212 Renaissance Italy & Global Mediterranean directly addresses Renaissance Italian art and Mediterranean connections, while MCCHEAM111 Introduction to Western Art History supplies broader European art-historical context. MCCLITR111 Introduction to Literary Studies, MCCLITR112 Great Literary Works, MCCLITR311 Film & Text and MCCLITR312 Perspectives on Literary Meaning provide literary methods; MCCMEDI111 Introduction to Film & Media supports film analysis; GOSHIST111 Modern History provides European historical context. MCCCOMM211 Style & Meaning examines linguistic choices in texts and HCBCOGN312 Psycholinguistics studies language processing, but neither teaches Italian. The workbook contains no Italian course, no cumulative Italian grammar, vocabulary, listening, speaking, reading or writing sequence, no study of Italian phonology, morphology, syntax, dialects or minority languages, no sustained Italian-language literary curriculum, and no Italian-language thesis preparation. The adjacent Renaissance, history, literature, film and language-science courses cannot substitute for the compulsory Italian-language disciplinary spine.

verified_module_credit_evidence.name: Medieval Literature of France and Italy: an 'histoire croisée'
prerequisites:
Voor toegang tot dit vak zijn geen specifieke vaardigheden vereist.

Studenten van de bachelors Franse taal en cultuur en Italiaanse taal en cultuur, de minor Middeleeuwen en vroegmoderne tijd, de minor Frans en de Franstalige wereld en de pre-masters Literary Studies en Linguistics hebben voorrang bij het volgen van dit vak. Andere studenten kunnen het vak volgen in het geval er plek is.

NB: dit vak bestaat uit wekelijkse hoorcolleges een aanvullende werkcolleges. Van alle studenten wordt verwacht dat ze aanwezig zijn bij de hoorcolleges. De werkcolleges, die in het derde uur van de colleges worden gegeven, spitsen zich afwisselend toe op Franse en Italiaanse literatuur. Het exacte schema wordt via Brightspace bekendgemaakt. Hierbij geldt:
\- studenten Frans zijn aanwezig bij de werkcolleges Frans \(die in de doeltaal gegeven worden\)\.
\- studenten Italiaans zijn aanwezig bij de werkcolleges Italiaans \(in het Nederlands\)\.
\- minor\- en keuzevakstudenten kiezen zelf voor werkcolleges in één van deze twee talen\. Deze keuze is tevens bepalend voor de toetsing\. Studenten van de minor Frans en de Franstalige Wereld volgen de werkcolleges Frans\.

prior_exception.reason: Leiden’s Korean Studies bachelor integrates a cumulative Korean-language sequence with Korean history, thought, culture, society, politics and region-specific methods. The chosen 180-EC pathway includes 65 EC of dedicated Korean-language and Korean-reading courses before the thesis (Korean 1–3, Korean Language in Use, Intermediate Korean Reading 1 and 2A, and Business Korean), and further Korean-centred seminars and primary-source work. UCR has no Korean-language course and no Korea-specific history, media, literature or politics course. A curriculum of 24 UCR courses drawn from broadly related social sciences and humanities would fail the requirement that each non-PPD course contribute concretely to the target-specific concept. It would conceal the central language and Korea-based source-training gap, so no defensible closest UCR alternative can be constructed.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The 2026–27 official catalogue shows first year 50 EC compulsory plus two 5-EC restricted choices; second year 20 EC compulsory and 40 EC specified restricted choices; third year a 5-EC compulsory thesis seminar, 15 EC of restricted language/topic study, a 10-EC final paper and 30 EC of free elective space. A single coherent option was selected in each restricted group. The programme-specific adopted OER confirms language progression from Korean 1 through Korean 3, further reading and final source-based work. No formal graduation route is named. All 180 EC are accounted for exactly once.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. No UCR course teaches Korean or specifically covers either Korea, Korean cultural sources or Korean history. GOSHIST111/211/312 cover modern history, empires and historical research without the Korean sequence; GOSPOLI112/212/313 address comparative politics, international relations and conflict without Korea-specific material. MCCMEDI111/211, MCCLITR111/311 and MCCHEAM111 can teach media, literature and art methods, but not Korean-language source reading or the Korea-centred historical and cultural curriculum. HCBCOGN312 examines psycholinguistics rather than Korean language acquisition. Those neighbouring methods do not sustain 23 substantively relevant non-PPD courses for a Korean Studies concept; semester feasibility cannot cure the subject mismatch.

prior_exception.reason: A valid 24-course UCR programme cannot represent this Latin American Studies bachelor’s defining combination of sustained Latin America-specific history, culture, politics, linguistics, Spanish/Portuguese language progression and study abroad. UCR has no Spanish or Portuguese language course or sequence, and only incidental Latin American examples within broader global courses. Filling 24 places with general history, politics, sociology, media or literature would change the target into general global studies and falsely imply regional and language preparation that UCR does not offer.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The 2026–27 Leiden curriculum has a 40-EC Latin American/linguistic first-year core plus 20 EC Spanish language, a second year with 10 EC compulsory core, 20 EC Spanish-speaking route content and a mandatory 30-EC study abroad, and a final year with 15 EC compulsory study, a 5-EC restricted choice, a 10-EC thesis and 30 EC open elective space. Spanish was selected as one internally coherent option; the alternative Brazil/Portuguese option likewise requires sustained region-specific language training. OER Article 2.2 says no formal graduation route, so routeSelection is null despite the study guide’s language-choice groups. The 2026–27 OER introduces a revised first year; later years here are the currently published guide structure and may change for later cohorts.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 rows of the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall-2026-cohort availability. The catalogue has Dutch (MCCCOMM112) but no Spanish or Portuguese language course. GOSHIST211 History of Empires, GOSPOLI212 Theory of International Relations, GOSPOLI313 Peace & Conflict and GOSSOCI214 Modern Sociology cover general comparative or colonial questions, not a sustained Latin American regional curriculum. GOSSOCI311 New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory mentions a Latin American civil-society case, but this is one example in a general global-sociology course. GOSHIST311 Native American Histories focuses on North America, not Latin America. MCCMEDI212 Media & the Environment treats Indigenous and postcolonial media generally. These courses could support selected adjacent questions, but they do not supply three years of Latin American history, culture, politics, language proficiency and the 30-EC abroad component. Their assembly into 24 courses would not be a defensible closest-match programme.

prior_exception.reason: A valid 24-course UCR programme cannot represent this Physics bachelor’s defining sequence of mechanics, electromagnetism, optics, quantum mechanics, statistical and solid-state physics, repeated experimental laboratories and a 27-EC independent physics research project. The current UCR catalogue contains mathematics, programming and energy/sustainability courses but no physics course sequence or physics laboratory. Filling the remaining places with adjacent mathematics, data science, engineering or sustainability courses would change the target into a different interdisciplinary programme and falsely imply foundational and advanced physics training that UCR does not provide.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The current official 2026–27 curriculum accounts for all 180 EC: 60 EC compulsory first year; 51 EC compulsory second year plus an instantiated 9-EC restricted physics choice; and 30 EC of instantiated physics core-package options, a separate 3-EC physics choice, and a 27-EC bachelor research project in year three. The programme has no named graduation route, so routeSelection is null. Its academic identity is sustained theoretical, mathematical and experimental physics rather than a collection of broadly science-related electives.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 rows of the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx, including course descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall-2026-cohort availability. UCR offers DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics, as well as DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming. Those courses provide useful mathematical and computational tools, but the catalogue contains no course in classical mechanics, electromagnetism, optics, quantum mechanics, statistical physics, solid-state physics, astrophysics or experimental physics, and no physics laboratory or physics research sequence. ENSSUST211 Energy & Sustainability and ENSSUST311 Renewable System Design concern energy systems and sustainable design rather than foundational physics. Even the strongest adjacent set therefore cannot give 23 non-PPD courses a concrete Physics rationale or reproduce the external programme’s theory–experiment progression.

prior_exception.reason: The current 2026–27 study product lists Core Curriculum: Humanities in a Digital World (module 5000VHDW2Y, 5 EC) as compulsory in both year one and year two. Counting that identical module twice would falsely satisfy the 180-EC requirement. The programme-specific OER confirms a curriculum change from September 2026 but does not establish which distinct 5-EC component replaces the duplicated second-year entry. A complete coherent comparator pathway therefore cannot be certified from the current official sources.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The supported unique curriculum totals 175 EC: 60 EC in year one, 55 additional unique EC in year two after counting Humanities in a Digital World only once, and 60 EC in year three comprising 10 EC advanced Dutch language acquisition, 10 EC instantiated linguistics-oriented choice, a 10-EC BA thesis and 30 EC open elective space. The programme’s defining Dutch-language progression and Dutch culture, history, literature and linguistics remain clear, but no-defensible-match evaluation requires a complete 180-EC comparator. Revisit the UCR-match decision once Leiden identifies the missing distinct 5-EC component or corrects the duplicate.

prior_exception.reason: A valid 24-course UCR programme cannot represent this professionally structured Notarial Law bachelor. UCR provides a small general law cluster, including private, criminal, constitutional, international, European and human-rights law, but it has no sustained sequence in property and real-estate law, matrimonial property, succession, family law, company structures for civil-law notaries, tax law, civil procedure or notarial drafting and practice. Filling the programme with politics, philosophy or general business courses would not reproduce the target’s defining private-law and civil-law-notary preparation.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The complete 180-EC comparator progresses from a 60-EC general legal foundation to 60 EC combining obligations, property, family, company, administrative and European law, and then to 60 EC dominated by matrimonial property, succession, notarial corporate structures, civil procedure, real-estate law, a notarial moot court and thesis. The public programme description likewise identifies real-estate, company, matrimonial-property and inheritance law as the third-year core. No route is selected.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 rows of the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall-2026-cohort availability. UCR offers GOSGATE102 Law, Society & Justice; GOSLAWJ111 Human Rights: Law & Philosophy; GOSLAWJ211 Criminal Law & Criminal Justice; GOSLAWJ212 Introduction to Public International Law; GOSLAWJ213 Comparative Constitutional Law; GOSLAWJ311 Principles of Private Law; GOSLAWJ312 Foundations of European Union Law; and BENBUSI311 Transnational Business Law. GOSLAWJ311 covers general obligations, tort and contract, and GOSGATE102 introduces property law, but there is no sequence in Dutch civil property law, conveyancing, real-estate law, matrimonial property, inheritance, family law, notarial company structures, tax law, civil procedure or notarial practice. Business and political-science courses can supply context, but cannot make 23 non-PPD courses substantively relevant to civil-law notarial training.

prior_exception.reason: Leiden's 180-EC South and Southeast Asian Studies pathway integrates 50 EC of progressive Hindi language and literature with regional history, cultures, religion, politics, economics, humanities methods, specialist seminars and a region-focused bachelor thesis. UCR offers no Hindi, Sanskrit, Tibetan or Indonesian language course and no South or Southeast Asian studies sequence. Its broadly comparative history, politics, philosophy, religion and literature courses could support occasional perspectives on the region, but they cannot make 23 non-PPD courses contribute concretely to a South and Southeast Asia-centred academic concept or reproduce the language-based cultural and source work that defines the Leiden degree.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The official 2026-27 curriculum totals exactly 180 EC: year one combines 30 EC of compulsory regional study with 20 EC of one language and two 5-EC restricted choices; year two combines 15 EC compulsory, 20 EC continued language, a 20-EC non-language specialisation and a 5-EC SSEAS elective; year three combines a 5-EC seminar, 15 EC of the selected Leiden pathway, a 10-EC BA thesis and 30 EC of genuine elective space. The selected Hindi and Modern South and Modern Southeast Asia pathway is coherent across all three years and preserves every component exactly once.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. The workbook contains no Hindi, Sanskrit, Tibetan or Indonesian course and no course dedicated to South or Southeast Asia. MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature includes isolated Indian literary examples, GOSPHIL214 Philosophy of Mind briefly considers Buddhist thought, and general history, politics, sociology, economics, religion, art and literature courses supply transferable disciplinary methods. Those isolated references and general methods do not constitute a regional language sequence, sustained area-study progression or region-specific source training. A 24-course UCR programme would therefore be built chiefly from adjacent global or comparative courses and would misrepresent the defining regional and linguistic core.

closed_findings: Restored the published 30-EC approved free-choice space instead of forcing one optional astronomy package
Retained required 8 EC and the distinct 18+1+3 EC research-project children without parent overlap
Corrected normalized instruction languages to NLD+ENG while preserving raw provenance
cases.ucr_reassessment: Separate UCR assessment required; superseded judgment preserved below.

prior_exception.reason: Leiden's Astronomy bachelor requires a continuous mathematical and physical foundation, dedicated astrophysics and planetary-systems study, practical observing and laboratory work, quantum mechanics, electrodynamics, stellar and galactic astrophysics, cosmology, specialist astronomy electives and a 22-EC independent astronomy research project. UCR offers useful mathematics, programming and data-science courses, but no astronomy or astrophysics course, no classical or quantum physics sequence, no astronomical observing course and no physics or astronomy laboratory. A 24-course response assembled from mathematics, computing, earth science and general natural science would replace Astronomy with adjacent tools and topics rather than implement its academic core.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The current official 2026-27 curriculum accounts for all 180 EC: a 60-EC compulsory first year; a 60-EC compulsory second year; and a third year containing 8 EC of required Radiative Processes and research integrity, a 22-EC bachelor research project, and a coherent instantiated 30-EC astronomy-centred elective package. The programme has no named graduation route. Its identity is a cumulative theory-observation-computation-research progression in astronomy, astrophysics, mathematics and physics.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics provide mathematical tools; DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming and the data-science sequence provide computational methods. ENSENVI111 Dynamic Earth addresses geology and geophysics, while other natural-science courses concern biology, chemistry, sustainability or engineering applications. The workbook contains no course in astronomy, astrophysics, planetary systems, classical mechanics, electromagnetism, optics, quantum mechanics, statistical physics or cosmology, and no astronomical observing or physics-laboratory sequence. The adjacent mathematical and computational courses cannot give 23 non-PPD courses a concrete Astronomy rationale or reproduce the external theory-to-research progression.

cases.ucr_reassessment: Separate UCR assessment required; superseded judgment preserved below.

prior_exception.reason: Leiden's Mathematics bachelor requires a cumulative proof-based sequence in mathematical structures, two courses each in analysis, linear algebra and algebra, followed by topology, complex function theory, measure theory, differential equations, probability and mathematical statistics, numerical mathematics, restricted advanced mathematics and an 18-EC independent mathematics project. UCR offers a useful but small applied mathematics and computing set. It has no course sequence in proof-based real analysis, abstract algebra, topology, measure theory, complex function theory or geometry and no independent mathematics research project. A 24-course response would therefore replace most of the degree's disciplinary core with computing, data science and adjacent applications.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The current official 2026-27 curriculum accounts for all 180 EC through a 60-EC first year, a 60-EC second year and a 60-EC third year. Restricted choices were instantiated by neutral official order before UCR provision was considered. The resulting route retains 36 EC of genuine open elective space and still contains a continuous 126-EC compulsory or restricted mathematics core plus the 18-EC bachelor project.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics provide applied calculus, linear algebra, numerical, systems and probability tools. DISARIN212 Logic & Discrete Mathematics adds formal and discrete reasoning, while DISARIN311 Optimization Methods in AI provides an adjacent optimisation application. The workbook contains no sustained proof-based analysis or algebra sequence, topology, measure theory, complex function theory, projective or differential geometry, number theory, stochastic-process sequence or mathematics bachelor project. Programming and data-science courses are useful tools but cannot turn the remaining 15 or more non-PPD slots into a coherent Mathematics degree or reproduce the external proof-to-research progression.

Voor dubbelstudenten Wiskunde en Informatica kan de succesvolle afronding van het Seminarium Presenteren en Communiceren hierbij vervangen worden door die van Research Methods in Computer Science. Van bovenstaande kan in bijzondere gevallen op schriftelijk en gemotiveerd verzoek van de student aan de Examencommissie worden afgeweken.

Voor de dubbele Bachelor programma's Wiskunde en Informatica, Wiskunde en Natuurkunde, en Wiskunde en Sterrenkunde gelden verder de regels van de andere studie met betrekking tot de verplichte voorafgaande onderwijseenheden.

### Verplichte voorkennis voor de onderzoeksprojecten

Deze wordt per onderzoeksproject (zie onder) gespecificeerd. 
Voor onderzoeksprojecten in de Algebra, Meetkunde of Getaltheorie zijn in ieder geval Algebra 1 en 2 vereist; Algebra 3 en Topologie worden aanbevolen. 
Voor de Analyse, Stochastiek en Besliskunde hangt dit van het onderzoeksproject af.

prior_exception.reason: Twente's Mechanical Engineering bachelor is an integrated engineering sequence in statics, mechanics of materials, thermodynamics, materials science, manufacturing, machine elements, dynamics, elasticity, tribology, fluid mechanics, heat transfer, control engineering, mechatronics, finite-element methods and production systems. These subjects support eight consecutive design, analysis and manufacturing projects before a mechanical-engineering research assignment. UCR offers useful mathematics, programming, product-design and sustainability courses, but it does not offer the mechanical-science core, engineering laboratory and workshop sequence, or progressive mechanical design and research sequence on which the degree depends. A 24-course response would be an applied mathematics, computing and sustainable-design programme, not Mechanical Engineering.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The official 2026-27 curriculum accounts for all 180 EC as twelve 15-EC modules. Years one and two contain eight compulsory integrated mechanical-engineering modules. Year three preserves 30 EC of genuine minor space and then requires Production Systems Engineering and the ME Bachelor Assignment. The programme has no named graduation route requiring selection.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics provide relevant quantitative tools, while DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming adds computing. BENENTR111 Consumer Product Design covers customer needs, fabrication planning, prototyping and sustainability; ENSSUST112 Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy and ENSSUST311 Renewable System Design address environmental impact and sustainable energy-system assessment. The workbook nevertheless contains no statics or mechanics-of-materials course; no thermodynamics, fluid-mechanics or heat-transfer sequence; no engineering materials, machine elements, manufacturing-process, elasticity, tribology, dynamics, mechatronics or finite-element course; and no mechanical-engineering laboratory, workshop, integrated design-project or bachelor-research sequence. The adjacent courses cannot supply a coherent 23-course non-PPD mechanical-engineering pathway.

prior_exception.reason: The Amsterdam VU-UT Mechanical Engineering bachelor builds four compulsory semesters around mechanics of materials, manufacturing and metals; thermodynamics and renewable-energy engineering; mass manufacturing, polymers, tribology, dynamics and vibrations; and systems, signal, control, precision and finite-element engineering. Its final compulsory semester then adds fluid mechanics, heat transfer, aerodynamic wind-tunnel work and an individual mechanical-engineering research assignment. UCR offers adjacent mathematics, computing, product-design and sustainability courses, but not this mechanical-science core or its laboratory, workshop, prototype, manufacturing and engineering-research progression. A 24-course response would not preserve the programme's academic identity as Mechanical Engineering.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The current official Amsterdam curriculum accounts for the 180-EC UT degree through six 30-EC semesters. Semesters one through four provide the compulsory mechanical-engineering sequence, semester five is genuine open minor space, and semester six is compulsory scientific research in mechanical engineering. This Amsterdam location has its own semester themes and course sequence rather than simply reproducing the Enschede modules, and it has no named graduation route requiring selection.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics provide relevant quantitative tools, while DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming adds computing. BENENTR111 Consumer Product Design covers customer-needs analysis, fabrication planning and prototyping; ENSSUST112 Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy and ENSSUST311 Renewable System Design address environmental impact and sustainable-energy assessment. The workbook contains no statics, mechanics-of-materials or elasticity course; no thermodynamics, fluid-mechanics or heat-transfer sequence; no metals, polymers, manufacturing, tribology, dynamics, vibration, precision-mechanism, control-engineering or finite-element course; and no mechanical-engineering laboratory, workshop, wind-tunnel, integrated design-project or graduation-research sequence. Linear Systems is a useful adjacent signals-and-systems course, but one such course cannot substitute for the semester-scale mechatronics and mechanical-design progression.

prior_exception.reason: Utrecht's Veterinary Medicine bachelor is a tightly integrated professional sequence in species-specific anatomy, embryology, physiology, pharmacology, infection and immunity, organ-system disease, animal nutrition, reproduction and obstetrics, veterinary public health, clinical diagnostics, anaesthesiology, surgery and animal-population epidemiology. Two longitudinal lines progressively develop veterinary clinical reasoning, practical skills and professional judgement, including practical work with living and dead animals, tissues and anatomical models. UCR offers valuable general biomedical, life-science, ecology, ethics and public-health courses, but it does not provide the species-specific veterinary science, clinical animal examination and treatment, surgery, reproduction, nutrition, animal-patient practicals or longitudinal veterinary clinician training on which the degree depends. A 24-course response would be a human-biomedical and ecology programme with animal-related context, not Veterinary Medicine.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The official current curriculum accounts for the complete three-year, 180-EC bachelor as three 60-EC years. Year one moves from mammalian and avian anatomy and embryology through molecular and cell biology, genetics, pharmacology, physiology, infection, immunity, haematology, circulation and respiration. Year two covers organ systems, nutrition across animal species, neurology, anaesthesiology, adaptation and welfare, plus 15 EC of open electives. Year three adds reproduction and obstetrics, veterinary public health and food safety, locomotion and clinical diagnostics, animal-population epidemiology and economics, a thesis, cross-organ disorders, surgery and 7.5 EC of open electives. Veterinaire clinicus and Veterinaire professional run through all three years; there is no named bachelor specialisation requiring route selection.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. HCBGATE101 Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, HCBLIFE211 Molecular Cell Biology, HCBLIFE212 Human Physiology, HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry, HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory, HCBBIOM311 Pharmacology, HCBBIOM312 Infection & Immunity and HCBBIOM313 Mechanisms of Disease provide a substantial general and human-biomedical base. HCBBIOM111 Epidemiology & Public Health, HCBLIFE311 Molecular Pathology & Genetics and HCBCOGN112 Neurobiology add population health, pathology, genetics and comparative-anatomy context. ENSECOL111 Introduction to Biodiversity, ENSECOL212 Ecosystems Uncovered, ENSECOL311 Marine Biology, ENSECOL312 Sustainable Farming & Innovation and GOSPHIL212 Ethics contribute ecology, animal biology, livestock systems, welfare-adjacent and animal-rights perspectives. The workbook nevertheless contains no comparative veterinary anatomy and organ-system sequence across mammal and bird species; no veterinary pharmacotherapy, diagnostics, anaesthesiology or surgery; no animal reproduction, obstetrics or species-specific nutrition; no food-production veterinary public-health training; and no practical progression with animal patients or longitudinal veterinary-clinician line. These are compulsory programme-wide gaps, not optional route differences.

prior_exception.reason: Utrecht's Pharmacy bachelor is a cumulative medicines-specific programme spanning pharmaceutical chemistry, dosage forms and administration, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, pharmacotherapy, drug research, product care, biological medicines and applied treatment across infection, neurology, hormonal disease, dermatology, psychiatry, cardiovascular disease, autoimmunity and oncology. Its longitudinal academic-skills requirements and bachelor thesis are developed within this pharmaceutical sequence. UCR offers a valuable general biomedical pathway and one dedicated Pharmacology course, but it does not offer pharmaceutical chemistry, drug formulation and product care, pharmacokinetics, dosage calculation and administration, clinical medication use and safety, or a sustained disease-specific pharmacotherapy sequence. A 24-course UCR response would therefore be a biomedical-sciences programme with one pharmacology course, not Pharmacy.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The official current curriculum accounts for all 180 EC through a 135-EC Farmacie major and 45 EC of genuine profiling space. The major comprises seven first-year medicines courses, ten advanced thematic pharmacy courses and a 7.5-EC bachelor thesis, with Academische Vaardigheden running longitudinally across all three years. The advanced curriculum is concentrically organised and applies prerequisites from first-year pharmacy study and specific level-2 courses to level-3 pharmacy courses.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. HCBGATE101 Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, HCBLIFE211 Molecular Cell Biology, HCBLIFE212 Human Physiology, HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry, HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory and HCBLIFE311 Molecular Pathology & Genetics provide life-science foundations. HCBBIOM311 Pharmacology directly studies drug targets, therapeutic use and toxicity; HCBBIOM312 Infection & Immunity and HCBBIOM313 Mechanisms of Disease add advanced biomedical applications. HCBBIOM111 Epidemiology & Public Health, HCBBIOM211 Functional Anatomy, HCBCOGN112 Neurobiology and HCBPSYC311 Medical & Health Psychology provide additional health context. The workbook nevertheless contains no dedicated pharmaceutical-chemistry sequence, no pharmaceutics or formulation laboratory, no pharmacokinetics or drug-metabolism course, no medicine-administration and dosage-calculation training, no product-care or clinical-pharmacy sequence, and no integrated pharmacotherapy progression across the compulsory disease areas. Those are programme-wide core gaps rather than missing optional specialisms.

prior_exception.reason: Utrecht's 180-EC Musicology pathway is defined by a compulsory sequence in notation and aural skills, harmony and form, music history before 1600, music from 1600 to 1900 and music from 1900 to the present, popular-music analysis and critical listening, music in screen media, advanced music analysis and criticism, music-theatre study and dedicated musicological research culminating in a Musicology thesis. UCR offers no course in music, music theory, aural skills, music history, music analysis or musicology. Its film, media, communication, literature, art, history and cultural-analysis courses can illuminate isolated social or media contexts around music, but they cannot make 23 non-PPD courses contribute concretely to a Musicology concept or reproduce the programme's defining disciplinary sequence. A 24-course UCR response would therefore be a media-and-culture degree with occasional musical examples, not a defensible Musicology curriculum.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The adopted 2026-27 curriculum totals exactly 180 EC: a 120-EC major and 60 EC of profiling space. The major contains 60 EC of compulsory first-year foundations, a 7.5-EC academic-context course, a 7.5-EC research seminar, a 7.5-EC bachelor thesis, one 30-EC advanced depth package and one 7.5-EC restricted choice. The selected first-listed Music and Society package comprises Music and Theatre, Music Analysis and Criticism, Music and Nature, and Dutch Music Cultures. The profiling space preserves an approved 30-EC profile package and 30 EC of genuine free choice without inventing subjects.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. The workbook contains no course whose disciplinary object is music or musicology and no course in notation, harmony, aural training, music history, music analysis, performance studies or musicological methods. MCCMEDI111 Introduction to Film & Media and MCCLITR311 Film & Text address film form and include sound among audiovisual elements; MCCMEDI212 Media & the Environment includes sound and digital media; MCCCOMM312 Creative Communication Laboratory treats rhythm and sound as poetic or conceptual material while expressly excluding music performance; MCCMEDI311 Media & Race, GOSHIST311 Native American Histories and several other cultural courses include music only as one example among broader media or artistic expressions. MCCMEDI312 The Documentary can include audio production. These are adjacent media, communication, literature and history offerings, not a musicological curriculum. They cannot supply a progressive theory-and-aural-skills sequence, sustained music history, advanced music analysis or a dedicated Musicology research trajectory, so constructing a 24-course comparison would misrepresent UCR's teaching.

prior_exception.reason: Utrecht's 180-EC Physics and Astronomy bachelor is defined by compulsory relativistic and classical mechanics, electromagnetism, astronomy and optics, quantum mechanics, statistical physics, three successive mathematical-techniques courses, experimental data acquisition, an experimental research project, advanced physics electives and a 15-EC physics research thesis. UCR offers useful supporting study in mathematics, programming, data science, Earth systems, climate and energy, but no course whose disciplinary object is physics or astronomy and no mechanics, electromagnetism, optics, quantum physics, statistical physics, thermodynamics or experimental-physics laboratory sequence. A 24-course UCR response would therefore be a mathematics/data/Earth-science programme adjacent to some physics applications, not a defensible Physics and Astronomy curriculum.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The current curriculum accounts for exactly 180 EC: Year 1 comprises six compulsory 7.5-EC foundations and 15 EC of physics choices; Year 2 comprises Quantum Mechanics, Statistical Physics, Mathematical Techniques 3 and Experimental Research Project plus 30 EC of physics choices; Year 3 comprises the compulsory 15-EC Bachelor Research/Thesis and 45 EC of advanced physics choices. The programme's published elective offer spans climate physics, experimental physics, theoretical physics, astronomy, quantum matter, field theory, subatomic physics, cosmology, fluid mechanics and biological/soft-matter physics. No formal route is imposed, so the genuine elective spaces remain unfilled rather than being assigned an invented specialization.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics provide substantial mathematical preparation. DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming, DISDATA111 Introduction to Data Science and related computing courses can support numerical work. ENSENVI111 Dynamic Earth, ENSENVI213 Earth System Science Tools, ENSSUST111 Climate Change, ENSSUST211 Energy & Sustainability and ENSSUST311 Renewable System Design address Earth, climate and energy applications. None is a physics or astronomy course. The workbook contains no classical or relativistic mechanics, electromagnetism, optics, quantum mechanics, statistical physics, thermodynamics, astrophysics, particle physics, condensed-matter physics, physics laboratory, experimental-physics research project or physics thesis sequence. Life Science Laboratory is specifically biological rather than physical. Filling 23 non-PPD places would therefore require extensive adjacent mathematics, computing, environmental science and engineering courses that cannot reproduce the programme's defining disciplinary core.
