prior_exception.reason: Utrecht Chemistry is defined by a compulsory first-year sequence in organic chemistry and spectroscopy, physical and inorganic chemistry, analytical chemistry, biochemistry, quantum chemistry, mathematics and physics, with extensive laboratory work. The selected Molecules and Materials pathway continues through physical, inorganic, solid-state, electrochemical, structural, spectroscopic, catalytic, organometallic, polymer, nano- and surface chemistry and ends in an individual chemistry research project. UCR has no chemistry gateway and no stand-alone progression in organic, inorganic, analytical, physical, quantum or synthetic chemistry. A 24-course UCR programme could combine biochemistry, environmental science, sustainability, mathematics and programming, but it would omit the target’s defining chemistry theory and multi-laboratory spine and would therefore misrepresent the degree.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The current public curriculum and its linked visual schedule account for exactly 180 EC: eight 7.5-EC compulsory first-year courses (60 EC), fourteen selected 7.5-EC post-first-year courses (105 EC), and a 15-EC ten-week individual bachelor thesis project. The first-listed Molecules and Materials path is instantiated with courses in molecular modelling, physical and organic chemistry, compulsory inorganic/solid-state chemistry, electrochemistry, structure determination, spectroscopy, catalysis, nanomaterials, organometallic and polymer chemistry, solids and surfaces, plus biochemical research methods. The live page is current as checked on 2026-09-28; its linked visual schedule remains labelled 2025–26 and the page cautions that offerings can change.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry and HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory provide biomolecular content and one broad biochemical/molecular laboratory course. HCBGATE101 and HCBLIFE211 cover cells and molecular life science. ENSGATE101/201 contain some general physics, chemistry and materials-science foundations; ENSENVI311 Environmental Biogeochemistry and ENSDELT311 R3: Recycling, Recovery, Remediation touch geochemical or inorganic processes and resource recovery; ENSSUST112 addresses life-cycle and circular-economy analysis. DISGATE102 and DISGATE101 supply mathematical and programming support. None provides a disciplinary chemistry sequence in organic synthesis, inorganic and solid-state chemistry, analytical measurement, thermodynamics and physical chemistry, quantum chemistry, molecular spectroscopy, catalysis, electrochemistry or materials characterisation, nor a progressive set of chemistry laboratories. These isolated biochemical, environmental and sustainability offerings cannot support 23 non-PPD courses with concrete relevance to a Chemistry concept or prepare a student for the target’s independent chemistry research project.

prior_exception.reason: Utrecht's programme is defined by a compulsory four-course Spanish-language acquisition sequence progressing from CEFR A1 to B2, followed by Spanish-medium and Spanish-specific study of sociolinguistics, morphosyntax, language change, intercultural communication, Spanish and Latin American literature, theatre, film, migration, colonial chronicles, cultural identity and historical memory. UCR's current curriculum contains no Spanish-language course and no course whose disciplinary object is Spanish language, Hispanic linguistics, Spanish or Latin American literature, or the cultures of Spain and Latin America. UCR literature, media, history, sociology and communication courses can illuminate isolated comparative themes, but they cannot supply the language competence on which the comparator's advanced courses and thesis depend. A 24-course UCR response would therefore be a broad literature, media and cultural-studies programme without Spanish, not a defensible closest match to Spanish Language and Culture.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The current 2026-entry curriculum totals exactly 180 EC: a 127.5-EC major and 52.5 EC of profiling space. The major contains 60 EC of compulsory first-year foundations, including 30 EC of progressive Spanish acquisition; 45 EC of Trans-Atlantic Perspectives depth study; a 7.5-EC methods course; a 7.5-EC professional/creative/academic writing course; and a 7.5-EC bachelor thesis. The standard Trans-Atlantic pathway is selected for the generic programme, while the optional Crossing Borders track is not combined with it. Genuine profiling space is preserved without inventing a minor or electives.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including course descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and Fall-2026 cohort scheduling. No course teaches Spanish language at any level, Spanish linguistics, Hispanic literature, or Spanish and Latin American cultural history as its sustained disciplinary object. MCCLITR111 Introduction to Literature, MCCLITR112 Texts & Worlds, MCCLITR212 Literature & Society, MCCLITR311 Film & Text and MCCLITR312 Contemporary Literatures offer transferable literary and cultural analysis; MCCMEDI111 Introduction to Film & Media, MCCMEDI211 Media Archaeology, MCCCOMM211 Intercultural Communication and MCCCOMM311 Persuasive Communication offer adjacent media and communication study; GOSHIST courses provide broad historical methods and selected regional themes; and GOSSOCI212 provides qualitative research. These courses could support comparative cultural work, but none develops Spanish speaking, listening, reading or writing, and none supports progression from A1 to B2 or prepares students to conduct advanced Spanish-language coursework and an independent thesis in the field. Because the missing language sequence is a prerequisite academic foundation rather than a peripheral specialty, 23 non-PPD UCR courses cannot form a coherent Spanish Language and Culture programme.

prior_exception.reason: Utrecht's ordinary Mathematics bachelor requires a cumulative proof-based core in calculus and linear algebra, analysis, abstract algebra, probability, multivariable analysis and topology, followed by restricted higher mathematics, a 15-EC mathematical thesis and additional advanced mathematical choice. UCR has a useful applied quantitative set but no proof-based sequence in analysis or abstract algebra, no topology or differential-geometry pathway, and no independent mathematics thesis. Even after using every directly relevant UCR mathematics course, most of the 23 non-PPD places in a UCR programme would have to be filled with computing, data science and applications that cannot substitute for this disciplinary progression. A 24-course alternative would therefore misrepresent the target rather than provide a defensible Mathematics programme.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The current formal programme accounts for all 180 EC as an 82.5-EC compulsory mathematical sequence, 7.5 EC of modelling, 15 EC of restricted Mathematics choice, 30 EC of further Mathematics choice and 45 EC of open profiling space. The required and selected major components still amount to 135 EC, including the 15-EC bachelor thesis. Choices were instantiated by official table order before UCR provision was assessed; the separate Mathematics & Applications direction was not substituted for the generic target.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned semesters. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods supplies applied calculus and linear-algebra tools; DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics provide valuable applied mathematical progression. DISARIN212 Logic & Discrete Mathematics adds formal and discrete reasoning, and DISARIN311 Optimization Methods in AI is a relevant application. The workbook does not contain a sustained proof-based real-analysis sequence, abstract algebra beyond introductory discrete material, topology, complex analysis, differentiable manifolds or a mathematics bachelor-thesis course. Programming, data-science, econometrics and AI courses support mathematical applications but cannot supply the missing disciplinary core or turn the remaining non-PPD course slots into a coherent Mathematics degree.

prior_exception.reason: The selected UvA pathway is defined by a cumulative Arabic-language sequence: Egyptian Arabic, Arabic script, Modern Standard Arabic, grammar, vocabulary, speaking, listening, reading and writing, followed by Arabic sociolinguistics, Arabic-medium literary study, a 30-EC Cairo semester, Arabic media and source interpretation, and a 12-EC thesis that combines Arabic competence with disciplinary analysis. UCR’s current catalogue contains no Arabic-language course at any level and no course whose sustained disciplinary object is Arabic linguistics or Arabic-language literature. UCR history, politics, religion, literature and media courses can illuminate isolated regional or comparative questions, but they cannot supply the language competence on which the advanced curriculum and thesis depend. A 24-course response would therefore be a broad humanities and regional-studies programme without Arabic, not a defensible closest match to Arabic Language and Culture.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The current official Major Arabische studies pathway accounts for exactly 180 EC: a 60-EC common first year, a 30-EC second-year taught sequence, a 30-EC Cairo semester, 18 EC of advanced third-year Arabic source/literature study, 30 EC of genuine free choice and a 12-EC bachelor thesis. The alternative Major Middle Eastern Studies is not combined with it. Genuine free choice remains open rather than being populated with invented electives.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows with course descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and Fall-2026 cohort scheduling. No course teaches Arabic speaking, listening, reading, writing, grammar or translation, and no course provides a sequence in Arabic linguistics or Arabic-language literature. MCCLITR111 Introduction to Literature, MCCLITR112 Texts & Worlds, MCCLITR212 Literature & Society, MCCLITR311 Film & Text and MCCLITR312 Contemporary Literatures provide transferable literary and cultural analysis; GOSHIST and GOSPOLI courses provide broad historical and political methods; GOSPHIL and GOSLAWJ courses address philosophy, religion and law; MCCMEDI and MCCCOMM courses support media and intercultural analysis. These subjects could support comparative work on society, culture and representation, but they do not establish the Arabic competence required for advanced Arabic-medium study, Arabic sources, the Cairo semester and the Arabic-focused thesis. Because the missing language sequence is the programme’s academic foundation rather than a peripheral specialty, 23 non-PPD UCR courses cannot form a coherent Arabic Language and Culture programme.

prior_exception.reason: The UvA programme devotes 138 specified EC to archaeological and ancient-world education before its separate 12-EC archaeology thesis, leaving 30 EC of genuine free choice. Required study spans archaeological sources and materials, prehistoric, Roman, medieval and early-modern European archaeology, environmental and scientific archaeology, digital archaeology, two credited field schools, excavation-to-publication training, field reporting, heritage and disciplinary theory. UCR has a small but valuable archaeology and heritage group—Introduction to World Archaeology, Greek Archaeology, and Heritage & Ancient Democracy—but no excavation-training sequence, archaeometric or archaeological-materials sequence, European prehistoric-to-medieval archaeology sequence, or archaeology thesis. Filling 24 UCR places mainly with history, art, cultural theory and generic methods would present neighbouring disciplines as an Archaeology bachelor. No defensible closest 24-course UCR programme can therefore be formed.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The current official curriculum totals exactly 180 EC: 60 EC of compulsory first-year study, 78 EC of compulsory later archaeology courses, 30 EC of open electives/minor/internship/study-abroad space and a 12-EC Bachelor Thesis Archaeology. The English trajectory represents the normalized bilingual target; the Dutch page shows the same curriculum structure. Genuine open choice is preserved without inventing electives.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and Fall-2026 cohort availability. MCCHEAM112 introduces world archaeology through material culture; MCCHEAM213 studies Greek archaeology; and MCCHEAM315 links ancient democracy, material evidence and heritage. MCCHEAM211, MCCHEAM212, MCCHEAM111, MCCHEAM312 and MCCHEAM316 contribute art, museum and heritage study, but do not replace archaeological method. GOSHIST courses provide historical analysis; GOSHIST213 includes ancient warfare but is not excavation archaeology. Environmental and data courses may support landscape or digital questions, yet no UCR sequence teaches archaeological stratigraphy, supervised excavation, finds processing, pottery/material identification, archaeometry, field reporting and an independent archaeology thesis. A 24-course archaeology-led programme cannot pass the specific course-to-concept and coherence gates.
